newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton up on mill buying, limited arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton up on mill buying, limited arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices moved up on the local market on Friday, dealers said, as fresh mill buying pushed prices up and limited arrivals kept offerings at a low ebb.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi moved up by 5/10 rupees at 870/925 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned lifted to 1,560/1,660 rupees per maund from 1,520/1,620 rupees.
F-414 moved up to 1,870/1,890 rupees per maund from 1,850/1,870 rupees while Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) lifted to 13,700/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 13,300/13,500.
"Arrivals of cotton at the producing centres remained low following unseasonal rain in some parts as well as end season consideration," one broker said.
"End of the cotton season is coming nearer and about 90 percent of the cotton crops is so far already marketed," he said.
